notes: Derived edit with derived-belief queries and a premise-route query. Derivability very_likely: the work-to-birthplace fact is almost never stated, both premises are stated everywhere (evidence). Change from the scouting, per the topic notes: the premise-route query now names the composer step explicitly ('First name the composer..., then give the city'), so it differs from the direct query; scoring is on the city, and the composer it names is diagnostic of the world. The scout's functional query ('Was the composer born in Salzburg?') is replaced because born_in carries no functional tag in RELATIONS.md; its slot asks whether the composer was born where the opera premiered (Vienna, 1791), which is yes in both worlds. Worlds: each revises one premise. 'The opera has a single composer' is treated as firm (K. 620, Mozart alone), so a two-composer world is not counted. Side facts go with each world: in w2 'The Magic Flute was Mozart's last opera' goes with P1. R1: 'the opera' is always said, since there are films (Bergman 1975, Branagh 2006) of the same name. R2 tension, as in the README's Elizabeth I example: in w2 the edit changes who 'the composer of The Magic Flute' refers to. Plausibility: Mozart lived, worked and died in Vienna, and the opera premiered there; 'Mozart was born in Vienna' occurs 95 times in Dolma (against 1,288 for Salzburg). Formal check (FINDINGS C3): the chains now state that a person is born in only one city, which both worlds' answers use.
